messages.subject: Re: facet_grid problem
parts:
Hi,

I am not an expert in this but usually I use : 

+facet_wrap(~MONTH) or facet_wrap(MONTH~.)

Did you try with facet_grid ? it may give you what you want.
For this one you can also use :  facet_grid(MONTH~.) 

Dorian.

2012/7/3 dhaval <nucle...@gmail.com>
Hi,

I am new to ggplot2 and have been trying to use fact_wrap but it does not seem to work. I've read online on the error and have tried all combinations of code, still no luck. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Here is a description of the output:

> names(braw)
[1] "AVG_PAYMENT"     "PASSING"         "SPECIALTY_GROUP" "MONTH"          (description of my data set)
> qplot(PASSING, AVG_PAYMENT, data = braw, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill = SPECIALTY_GROUP, position="dodge")  (this works but not I want to add a facet_wrap over different months)
> qplot(PASSING, AVG_PAYMENT, data = braw, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill = SPECIALTY_GROUP, position="dodge")+facet_wrap(factor(braw$MONTH))
Error in layout_base(data, vars, drop = drop) : 
  At least one layer must contain all variables used for facetting (does not work)
> qplot(PASSING, AVG_PAYMENT, data = braw, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill = SPECIALTY_GROUP, position="dodge")+facet_wrap(factor(MONTH))
Error in factor(MONTH) : object 'MONTH' not found (neither does this)
> qplot(PASSING, AVG_PAYMENT, data = braw, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill = SPECIALTY_GROUP, position="dodge")+facet_wrap(factor(MONTH))
Error in factor(MONTH) : object 'MONTH' not found (not even without the dodge)

I'm not sure what is wrong.I tried permutations of ~. in the facet_wrap too but in vain...

Thank you,

Dhaval
